question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using the Complement
question.problem: Given that $X∼B(7,0.5),$ compute $P(X\le 6).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(7,0.5),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x})(0.5)^{x}(0.5)^{7-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X\le 6)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,…,6.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X>6)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=7,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X>6),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6) & =P(X\in \{7\}) \\  & =f(7) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{7})(0.5)^{7}(0.5)^{7-7} \\  & =(0.5)^{7} \\  & ≈0.0078\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 6) & =1-P(X>6) \\  & ≈1-0.0078 \\  & =0.9922\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.

judgment.reasoning: Each answer is independently supported by its own captured worked solution and agrees with the earlier answer. For q-97519, the binomial formula gives P(X=5)+P(X=6)=21(0.9)^5(0.1)^2+7(0.9)^6(0.1)=0.4960116, rounding to 0.4960. For q-97516, P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5)=0.08192+0.01536+0.001536=0.098816, rounding to 0.0988. For q-97521, the complement gives P(X≤6)=1-P(X=7)=1-(0.5)^7=0.9921875, rounding to 0.9922. MA rounds the complement first in the last solution, but obtains the same correctly rounded final answer.
